Bryn Shander

Friendliness ❄❄❄   Services ❄❄❄   Comfort ❄❄❄

The first stop for most visitors to Icewind Dale, Bryn Shander is a walled town perched atop a cold, lonely, wind-lashed hill. Bright lanterns suspended over narrow streets twist in the wind. The walls stand 30 feet high — two concentric rings of upright wooden poles with dirt and rubble packed between them. Gates are closed when it's dark outside, which is to say more often than not.

Detail
Population1,200
LeaderSpeaker Duvessa Shane (lawful good human noble) — young, sharp, head of the Council of Speakers
SheriffMarkham Southwell (lawful good human veteran) — commands the militia, actively working to delegitimize Auril worship
Militia250 tribal warriors + 20 veterans
Sacrifice to AurilHumanoid — lottery system
RivalriesNone
Available QuestFoaming Mugs (completed)

Key Locations

  • Blackiron Blades — Garn the Hammer's smithy + Elza's outfitter. Cheapest blades in Ten-Towns. Party has 10% discount (Foaming Mugs reward).
  • House of the Morninglord — Shrine of Amaunator run by Mishann (neutral good priest). Copper Knobberknocker rents the attic.
  • The Northlook — best inn for adventurers. Scramsax (neutral human veteran) runs it. Ol' Bitey the enchanted stuffed trout is above the hearth.

Bal's Grove

Bal is Rhystal's Emerald Enclave contact in Bryn Shander. He tends a hidden grove tucked behind the city wall — small, stubborn, and improbable, the kind of thing that shouldn't exist this far north. Rhystal has been helping him keep it alive.

Bal takes Rhystal by the arm before the others can follow. The hidden grove is tucked behind the city wall, small and stubborn and improbable — the kind of thing that shouldn't exist this far north. Except one corner of it is wrong. The leaves don't just die here, they freeze mid-fall. The ice that covers them isn't grey like the rest of Icewind Dale's ice. It's blue-white. Deliberate. Like a signature.

Bal doesn't know what caused it. He just knows it happened overnight and felt like something chose to do it — not weather. He's shaken. He's been tending this grove for years and something touched it last night that he didn't see and couldn't stop.

He asks Rhystal what they've been seeing out there. He wants to know if this is happening elsewhere. He suspects it is.

DM — What This Means:

  • The blue-white ice is Auril's influence — not natural cold, but intentional killing. Auril is killing things that shouldn't be killable. Not with cold. With intention.
  • This was first introduced in Session 7 (Phase 5) as a seed — Rhystal has seen this already. It has not yet been resolved.
  • The Summer Star in the party's pack needs a unicorn horn to activate. Bal's dying grove is the first hint of why that matters — the natural world is being systematically killed by Auril's cult.
  • Ravisin (the frost druid behind the Bremen lake monster and the White Moose) has been doing this to groves across Icewind Dale. She may not know about this one yet.
  • If Auril is ultimately defeated, this grove recovers. A powerful closing image for Rhystal's arc.

Copper Knobberknocker (rock gnome acolyte of Lathander, attic of the House of the Morninglord) has also noticed the dying grove. He's been watching it from a distance, praying over it. He doesn't know Bal. He doesn't know about Rhystal's Enclave connection. But he will mention Ravisin if the party talks to him — he's heard reports from Lonelywood of a frost druid killing every living thing she can find.

Foaming Mugs (Completed)

The party retrieved the Battlehammer iron ingots from the goblins and delivered them to Blackiron Blades. Reward: 10% discount at Blackiron Blades (permanent).

DM: The goblins were from Karkolohk — the goblin fortress north of Ten-Towns. The polar bears pulling their wagon are a potential ally or complication if the party ever travels that direction. Izobai (the one-eared goblin boss) escaped if she wasn't killed.

Cult of Auril in Bryn Shander

DM: Despite being the largest town, the cult has been told to lay low here. Jelenneth Arnuanna is the icebringer representing the Church of Auril in Bryn Shander. She's instructed the 50 or so cultists living here to be inconspicuous.

Why? Sheriff Markham Southwell has been working with Mishann (of the House of the Morninglord) to delegitimize the worship of Auril. Copper Knobberknocker, also at the shrine, is a secondary irritant to cult operations — his devotion to Lathander and his tending of the hidden grove are direct philosophical opposition to everything the Cult of Auril represents.

The cult safehouse is located across from Blackiron Blades. Low-ranking cult members often buy weapons from Garn the Hammer — his cheap blades are popular with spites who want to arm themselves without drawing attention.

Humanoid sacrifice lottery: Bryn Shander performs humanoid sacrifice. The lottery is the darkest open secret in town — most residents accept it as the price of Auril's grudging tolerance. Markham hates it but hasn't found a way to stop it without triggering a cult backlash.
